simple.meaning: מַקָּבָה (maqqâbâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, a perforatrix , i.e. a hammer (as piercing ).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מַקָּבָה (H4717) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Kings 6:7, with occurrences in 1 Kings, Isaiah, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַקָּבָה (H4717) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מַקָּבָה (H4717) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מַקָּבָה (maqqâbâh) / H4717 is traced through 1 Kings 6:7, Isaiah 44:12, Jeremiah 10:4 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H4717. maqqebeth I. מַקֶּ֑בֶת noun feminine hammer (by means of which one drives in nails and pegs); — absolute ׳מ Judg 4:21 (+ יָתֵד ); elsewhere plural מַקָּבוֺת 1Kin 6:7 (+ גַּרְזֶן ); Isa 44:12 ; Jer 10:4 (+ מַסְמְרוֺת ). — On name Maccabee see Schü Geschichte. i. 158 .
